findings.failure_scenario: Bloom.of(ordinals, m, k) does not validate m before use: with m<=0 and a non-empty ordinals collection, Math.floorMod(combined, m) throws a raw ArithmeticException instead of the canonical constructor's IllegalArgumentException("m is a positive multiple of 8: ...") -- the same bypass-the-canonical-constructor pattern round 1 fixed for k, not extended to m. Low current risk: m is always test-supplied and positive today; M2.6 hasn't landed to compute it from a real budget yet.

Bloom.of() does not reject negative ordinals even though mightContain() now does: Bloom.of(Set.of(-1,2,3), 32, 3) succeeds silently, but a later mightContain(-1) on that same filter throws instead of returning true for a value that was a member at construction time -- a write/read asymmetry this round's own fix introduced. Low current risk: ordinals only ever come from the non-negative IndexOrdinalRegistry today.
